records.rationale: Both paths and full helper/init code reviewed. Retain ordered background filesystem sync, atomic pending count and five-jiffy wakeup polling so wake events can abort waiting without waiting for sync completion. All callers serialize on the native system transition mutex, so the work_pending/queue count decision has one producer; worker may finish concurrently and a running item may be queued for one further sync. Background sync continues on EBUSY; successful return requires the count to reach zero. Existing native sync helper, configuration and allocation-failure cleanup remain. This is generic Android runtime responsiveness, not a future device feature.

records.rationale: All three paths reviewed. Retain current generic snapshot transform/init/post-save and map-write-control source hooks. security: Do not retain ACK removal of native suspend-statistics locking. Native control flow and permission/lock guards remain in the reviewed PM adaptations. Filesystem-sync wait may abort while background sync continues; this improves responsiveness but is not proof of durable storage on an aborted attempt. Resume callback failures become retryable. QoS skip/rewrite hooks deliberately delegate constraint policy to trusted modules and may weaken thermal/power constraints when used. Snapshot transformation hooks supply no implemented crypto/error protocol and cover only uncompressed data, so no hibernation confidentiality/integrity claim is justified. ARM64 bootloader and disabled physical genpd integration are excluded; generic source interfaces in configured SDK subsystems are retained conservatively.
